lsp_envelope_skew_statement.what_changed: the daemon auth envelope key is now `_mpd` on both sides — the reader/stripper (params["_mpd"] then `delete cleanParams["_mpd"]`) and the three writer sites — all in the same artifact, which also spawns the daemon (`spawnDaemonProcess` runs this same cli.js with the `daemon` argument).
lsp_envelope_skew_statement.already-running_daemon_behaviour: the daemon lives under ~/.mpd/lsp-daemon/v<version>/ (socket, daemon.pid, daemon.auth, daemon.log). ensureDaemonRunning() first PROBES the running daemon by writing `mpd/ping` with the renamed envelope and a 500 ms budget; a pre-rename daemon does not recognise the new key, answers the auth error (`daemon_authentication_failed`) instead of a ping result, and the probe therefore fails. The client then SPAWNS a fresh daemon and waits up to 5000 ms for reachability; if the stale process still owns the socket, that wait times out and the caller sees `LSP daemon did not become reachable at <socket>` (surfaced as daemon-unreachable with the 'auto-started on demand and will be retried' hint). The version directory is keyed on the packaged daemon version, which this rename does NOT change, so a stale process can share it.
lsp_envelope_skew_statement.remedy: stop the stale daemon once — `kill $(cat ~/.mpd/lsp-daemon/v<version>/daemon.pid)` (or delete that version directory) — then retry; the client auto-starts a clean daemon. Restarting dsh alone is NOT sufficient while the old daemon process is alive.

deviations_and_findings.D-1 sc-gb's literal residual vs the wave: t13's sc-gb prescribes adding the literal retired env-key spelling to the git-bash residual list. That literal is exactly what the wave's frozen acceptance greps forbid in shipped files (G5: `grep 'OMO_CODEX'` over every shipped file = 0 lines; the task's verify 2: `git grep -E 'OMO_CODEX|_omo'` over these three files = no output). I resolved it by (a) expressing the two literal-bearing deletion transforms as structural RegExps, (b) writing the lsp envelope pattern the way this file's own BRAND_TOKEN_RE writes it (`/_(?:om)o/g` — an underscore followed by the omo shape, so the retired key is never spelled), and (c) keeping the git-bash residual literal as the artifact's own name only. Protection is NOT weakened: BRAND_ALLOWLIST is now empty, so assertBrandClean fails loudly on ANY brand-shaped token in the artifacts (proved by the negative control), which strictly subsumes a literal residual.
deviations_and_findings.D-2 new scrub mechanism: applyMpdScrub now accepts RegExp entries in `replace`/`residual` (2 lines). A literal-pair table cannot delete a foreign key without naming it, and naming it is what the acceptance greps forbid.
